what_was_done: _LITERAL_PATHSPECS in commits.py now forces the other three global pathspec settings off with literal on ({GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS: 1, GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS: 0, GIT_NOGLOB_PATHSPECS: 0, GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS: 0}); gitrun's full.update(env) lets the zeros override a person's 1s, so git no longer exits 128 ('literal' incompatible with all other global pathspec settings) when GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS=1 or GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS=1 is inherited. The finding's other git-environment question answered in the same places: the repository-locating keys (GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES, GIT_COMMON_DIR) are stripped for every call by gitrun._REPO_LOCATING_KEYS, now pinned by a test; GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/SYSTEM and the author and committer variables pass through by design and only shape the commit's metadata (test_flush_without_git_identity already covers identity). Tests in test_state_commits.py: test_flush_with_conflicting_pathspec_environment monkeypatches GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS=1 and GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS=1 into os.environ, flushes a valid [ab].md beside an over-cap a.md, and asserts committed-not-failed, a.md rejected and out of HEAD, and a clean later flush; test_flush_ignores_inherited_repo_locating_environment sets GIT_DIR to a foreign bare repo plus GIT_WORK_TREE and GIT_INDEX_FILE and asserts the state branch advances, the foreign index is never created and the foreign repo receives nothing. Verified the first test fails with GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS forced to 1 in the dict (flush returns failed). Spec: topics/state-commits.md step 4 now says the other global pathspec settings are forced off and why.
